### context: full
FORGING COST INPUT RULES:
  Lines marked deterministic are computed from the measured geometry and will REPLACE whatever you return for them — restate them, do not re-derive them.
  Lines marked UNDECIDED are yours to answer: nothing in the geometry settles them. Answer from the drawing, the photo or the part name, and say which you used.
  materialId=mat-al6082-forge  [1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer); aluminium → mat-al6082-forge (representative forging billet — not a drawing callout) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  grade: UNDECIDED — needs "Which aluminium grade?" (6082 (Al Forging Stock) | 6061 (Al Forging Stock) | 2014 (Al-Cu forging stock — aero and automotive) | 7075 (Al Forging Stock) | 2618 (Al-Cu Piston/Aero) | 7050 (Al-Zn Aero Forging Stock))
  partWeightKg=2.851  [2.800 kg finished + 18.8 cm³ of holes drilled from solid (≤ Ø25; larger bores pierced) + 0.0 cm³ machining stock (2 mm a side on the machined faces, closed-die) — 1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  process=closed-die  [aluminium at 100,000/yr — closed-die impression forging is the volume workhorse: net-shape grain flow, good tolerance, lowest piece cost once dies amortise [tolerance class, safety-critical assumed — confirm before quoting] — deterministic, use verbatim]
  projectedAreaCm2=288.4  [estimated: bbox face × √fill for a solid, bbox face for a shell below 5% fill (no measured silhouette) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  shapeComplexity=moderate  [score 1 + 0 + 1 = 2 → moderate — 1 for 4 free-form face(s), 0 for 2 undercut face(s), 1 for 120 faces (≥ 3 complex, ≥ 1 moderate; free-form ≥ 3 / ≥ 8, undercuts ≥ 4, faces ≥ 120 — CostVision heuristic) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  yieldFraction=0.743  [closed-die stock yield band 0.55–0.8, midpoint 0.675 — as-forged weight ÷ billet, CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; the 10% flash is itemised, so yieldFraction = 0.675 × 1.10 = 0.743; billet = 2.851 kg forging + 0.285 kg flash = 3.136 kg ÷ 0.743 = 4.221 kg; finished ÷ billet = 2.800 kg ÷ 4.221 kg = 0.66; 4.221 − 3.136 = 1.085 kg is scale, crop and any pierced wad (not itemised) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  flashAndScaleKg=0.285  [10% of the 2.851 kg forging, squeezed out at the flash land (CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced) — cost-neutral: the yield is scaled by the same fraction, so the billet stays forging ÷ 0.675 — deterministic, use verbatim]
  forgeId=forge-press-1600t  [Kt 5 for a moderate shape, σflow 55 MPa hot flow stress for aluminium (both CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced); A = 288.4 cm² silhouette + 57.10 cm² flash land = 345.50 cm²; F = Kt × σflow × A = 5 × 55 MPa × 34,550 mm² ÷ 9,806.65 N/t = 969 t × 1.2 safety = 1163 t → the smallest forge press at or above it: the 1,600 t press (library presses 500, 1,600, 2,500, 4,000, 8,000 t) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  strokesToForm=3  [3 hit(s): 2 impression(s) + 1 extra finisher hit(s), moderate shape; takt = 3 s billet from the heater + 3 × 4 s mechanical press hit + transfer = 15 s (load and hit times CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  timePerBlowSec=4  [hit + transfer on the press (informational — the cycle below is the line takt) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  cycleTimeHr=0.004167  [3 hit(s): 2 impression(s) + 1 extra finisher hit(s), moderate shape; takt = 3 s billet from the heater + 3 × 4 s mechanical press hit + transfer = 15 s (load and hit times CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced). Not costed: billet cut-off (saw / shear) and the billet heater's capital — the rate book has no billet saw, bar shear or induction heater (the heating energy is costed) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  labourId=lab-uk-forge  [forge-shop operative — deterministic, use verbatim]
  manning=2  [closed-die line crew: forger + heater / handler — engineering typical — deterministic, use verbatim]
  rejectRate=0.02  [2% forging scrap (laps, underfill, cracks at inspection) — engineering typical — deterministic, use verbatim]
  furnaceType=gas  [aluminium forges warm — billets soak in a gas furnace — deterministic, use verbatim]
  trimMachineId=press-100t  [flash line 4.4 √A = 747 mm and flash 0.015 √A = 2.55 mm over A = 28,840 mm² (outline and thickness after ASM closed-die practice); 747 mm × 2.55 mm × 55 MPa hot flow stress ÷ 9,806.65 N/t = 10.7 t × 1.25 margin = 13.38 t → the 100 t press, the smallest mechanical press in the library at or above it (flow stress CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; a pierce in the same stroke is not added to the force) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  trimCycleHr=0.004167  [the trim press stands in line and works to the forge takt (15 s) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  trimLabourId=lab-uk-forge  [forge-shop operative — deterministic, use verbatim]
  trimManning=1  [one operator on the in-line trim press — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieSteel=h13  [H13 — the impression-die workhorse — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieImpressions=2  [blocker + finisher — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieCostGBP=45724  [2-impression h13 die over 288.4 cm²: Die design & CAM 65.3 h £3,814 + Die blocks (both halves + holder allowance) 446 kg £4,233 + Block prep (squaring, faces, keyways) 52.3 h £2,738 + Die sinking × 2 impression(s) 302 h £15,813 + EDM (deep ribs, tight radii) 75.5 h £4,410 + Harden + temper the blocks £3,480 + Impression polishing × 2 32 h £1,450 + Die tryout — 3 sessions 18 h £1,541 = £37,479; toolmaker overhead + profit at 22% of it = £8,245; die set £37,479 + £8,245 = £45,724 (toolroom hours and the die-block rules are CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; rates from the toolroom book); the kernel's face-count die £63800 is not used — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieLife=64728  [size factor (100 ÷ 288.4 cm²)^0.2 = 0.809098; 80,000 forgings a die set for aluminium × 1 moderate impression × 0.809098 size = 64,728 forgings — CostVision engineering-typical figures, not sourced; die sets are charged fractionally over the programme — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatingEnergyKwhPerKg=0.18  [energy to bring aluminium to forging temperature, wall-plug at an induction heater — CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; charged on every billet heated: 0.18 kWh/kg × 4.221 kg billet ÷ 0.98 for the 2% scrap = 0.775 kWh a good part, priced at the costing book's tariff (gas furnace × 2.4 kWh of gas) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatTreatCostPerKg=1.2  [solution-age for a aluminium forging: £1.2/kg × the 2.851 kg forging, bought-in (UK price × the country's heat-treat factor — CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  descaleCostPerKg=0.12  [forge scale removed after the trim, before MPI and machining (shot blast or pickle): £0.12/kg × the 2.851 kg forging — the flash is off by then — UK price × the country's process-service factor, CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ndtCostPerPart=0  [not safety-critical — no NDT — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finish question: UNDECIDED — needs "Is the part coated or surface-treated?" (None — bare part | Sulphuric anodise (aluminium) | Powder coat (iron phosphate pre-treat))
